privacy.metaDescription: What ReadAware stores, what leaves your device, and the choices you control: local-first data, end-to-end encrypted sync, bring-your-own-key AI.
privacy.body:
# Privacy Policy

*Last updated: September 20, 2026*

ReadAware is a local-first reading app. Books and reading data are stored on your device. Optional sync is end-to-end encrypted. Optional AI sends relevant text to a model provider, directly with your own key or through our relay with built-in AI. The app has no ads or analytics; website measurement is described separately below.

This policy covers the ReadAware apps and the readaware.app website ("we" is the ReadAware developer). For any question or request, write to [hi@ahpx.me](mailto:hi@ahpx.me).

## On your device

Everything the app works with — imported books, highlights, notes, reading progress and statistics, preferences, and the app's internal event log — is stored locally on your device. None of it is uploaded unless you enable one of the optional features below. Diagnostic logs are plain local files: they record technical events, never the text of what you read, and they leave your device only if you explicitly send a diagnostic report.

## Sync — optional

If you connect a sync account:

- **Account data.** Your email address identifies the account and receives sign-in links (delivered through our email provider, Resend). Alongside it we keep technical account records: plan tier, storage used, and session data.
- **Your content is end-to-end encrypted.** The synced event log and your book files are encrypted on your device, with a key derived from a passphrase only you know, before anything is uploaded. Our server stores ciphertext: we cannot read your books, highlights, or notes. If the passphrase is lost, we cannot recover the data — that is the point.
- **Operating the service**, the server necessarily processes standard connection metadata — IP address, timestamps, object sizes — for delivery, quotas, and abuse prevention. The sync relay runs on Cloudflare infrastructure.
- Prefer your own storage? A transport plugin (for example WebDAV) syncs the same encrypted envelopes to a server you control, and our relay is never involved.

## Payments — optional

Paid plans are processed by Stripe under Stripe's own privacy policy. We never see your card details; we receive the email you paid with, the plan, and the subscription status.

## AI — optional

AI features run after you configure them. With your own API key, relevant selections, passages, questions, and context go directly to your selected provider under its terms. Your key is encrypted on your device. Built-in AI instead forwards these requests through our relay to the upstream model provider over TLS. The relay processes plaintext to forward requests and meter usage, but does not persist request or response content. The model provider processes the text under its own terms. Sync encryption does not make AI requests end-to-end encrypted to you alone.

## Web search and images — optional

If you enable web search, queries and requested page URLs are sent to the search provider you select, using your own provider key. Search and page reading use that same provider where supported. These requests are separate from encrypted sync and are processed under the search provider's terms.

Displaying an image preview can download a public image into the app's local cache; the image host receives the network request and associated connection metadata. When image content is included in an AI request, it is sent to your selected model provider. Image input depends on the model's capabilities.

## Local API — optional

The local API is disabled by default. When enabled, it listens only on this computer and requires a separate access token. It lets an authorized assistant read library metadata, book text, annotations, reading records, and scoped memory while ReadAware is running. It does not provide write operations or expose settings, model keys, or raw files.

You choose which assistant receives the connection token. That assistant may send retrieved data to its own provider; review its configuration and terms before connecting it. Resetting the token invalidates previous tokens, and disabling the API stops local access. These actions cannot recall data another assistant has already received.

## Diagnostic reports — optional

If something breaks, you can send us a diagnostic report from the app. It contains the app's technical logs (no reading content) and is stored with the app version, platform, and a hashed IP address, used solely to debug the problem.

## Deleting your data

- Local data is yours to delete with the app.
- **Settings → Data & Sync → Delete account** permanently removes your account, the synced event log, and every uploaded file from our server, and cancels any active subscription.
- For any data request beyond that, email [hi@ahpx.me](mailto:hi@ahpx.me).

## The website

readaware.app is served by Cloudflare Workers and Static Assets. We use cookie-free Cloudflare Web Analytics for aggregate traffic and performance, and a first-party endpoint backed by Cloudflare Analytics Engine for landing entries and download clicks. The latter records only a coarse source category (such as Google, Bing, ChatGPT, GitHub, or direct), public landing/current page paths, and the selected release asset, platform and advertised release version. It does not record IP addresses, identifiers, raw referrers, query strings, fragments, email addresses, or reading content. Session storage keeps the source category, landing page and expiry for a 30-minute attribution window, without a visitor ID. Both measurements respect Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control; sign-in pages are excluded. Click counts are not installations or unique people. Cloudflare still processes connection metadata to deliver and protect the site.

## Children

ReadAware is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

## Changes

When this policy changes, we will update this page and the date above; meaningful changes are also called out in the release notes.

overview.metaDescription: Read, annotate, use AI, protect your library, and build ReadAware desktop plugins with the current development API.
overview.body:
# Documentation

ReadAware brings your books, annotations, conversations, and reading memory together in a local-first desktop app. Reading and organizing your library work without an AI account. Connect your own model provider, or an available ReadAware AI plan, when you want the assistant.

## Start reading

- [Download and install](/docs/install) — choose a desktop package and understand updates.
- [Getting started](/docs/getting-started) — import books, adjust the reader, use AI and web search, connect another assistant, and protect your data.

## Build with ReadAware

Plugins can navigate books, work with annotations and memory, extend the assistant, and compose host services. Start with a task, then find the public contracts that support it.

- [Plugin system](/docs/plugins) — domains, contributions, services, and trust boundaries.
- [Build a plugin](/docs/plugins/develop) — a small working plugin and the desktop development loop.
- [Capabilities Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) — search capabilities and API methods, inspect permissions, and copy manifest fragments.
- [API reference](/docs/plugins/api) — scopes, lifecycle, state changes, resources, background work, and composition.
- [Publishing](/docs/plugins/publishing) — package, review, and submit your plugin.

## Documentation and app versions

These guides describe the current development build, including features that may arrive after the latest published app. Plugin reference pages follow the current development contract, and the latest published app can expose earlier capability versions. Check the Explorer and your installed app's `ctx.capabilities`; declare the versions your plugin actually needs in `manifest.json`.

Downloads and release notes are maintained on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest). For support, use [GitHub issues](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/issues) or [Discord](https://discord.gg/whDrKXwHWU).

install.metaDescription: Install ReadAware on macOS, Windows, or Linux, choose the right package, and check release notes and update channels.
install.body:
# Download and install

This guide covers ReadAware desktop on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Choose a package below, or check the assets and requirements on the [latest release](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest). Download links follow the latest stable release; development API documentation may be newer than that release.

## macOS

- [Apple Silicon .dmg](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-macos-arm64.dmg)
- [Intel .dmg](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-macos-x64.dmg)

Open the disk image and drag ReadAware into Applications. Use Apple Silicon for M-series Macs and Intel for Intel Macs. The release pipeline signs and notarizes macOS packages. If macOS reports a damaged or unverifiable download, download it again from the official release page and check that release's notes before changing security settings.

## Windows

- [Windows x64 installer](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-windows-x64-setup.exe)
- [Portable ZIP](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-windows-x64-portable.zip)

Run the installer, or extract the portable archive and open ReadAware. Windows builds are not currently OS code-signed. If SmartScreen appears, first verify that the file came from the official release. You can then choose **More info → Run anyway** if you trust the download.

## Linux

- [AppImage](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-linux-x64.AppImage)
- [Debian / Ubuntu package](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-linux-x64.deb)
- [RPM package](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/releases/latest/download/ReadAware-linux-x64.rpm)

Make the downloaded AppImage executable, then open it. For the stable alias filename:

```bash
chmod +x ReadAware-linux-x64.AppImage
./ReadAware-linux-x64.AppImage
```

An AppImage may need your distribution's FUSE compatibility package. If it will not start, use the matching native package and review the release requirements.

## Updates

Settings → About contains update checks and the Stable / Beta channel choice. Automatic checking is controlled in Settings → General. Follow the app's update prompt; installation may require a restart. Desktop updater signatures are separate from OS code signing.

After an upgrade, the what's-new dialog shows the version highlights and links to the project on GitHub and Discord. You can continue reading immediately, or turn this dialog off in Settings → General. The same community links remain available in Settings → About.

Keep a backup before moving between versions or trying a development build. [Getting started](/docs/getting-started) explains backup and sync.

## Other release artifacts

Some published releases include mobile artifacts. Their availability and instructions belong to the specific release notes; the desktop plugin contracts in this documentation do not establish mobile support or feature parity.

## Next

[Import your first book](/docs/getting-started), or [build a plugin](/docs/plugins/develop) against the app version you have installed.

gettingStarted.metaDescription: Import and read books, connect AI and web search, share reading context through the local API, and understand offline sync and encrypted backups.
gettingStarted.body:
# Getting started

Start with one book. AI, sync, and plugins can be configured when you need them. This guide describes the current development build; some controls may not yet be available in the latest published app. Check your installed version in Settings → About.

## Import a book

Use the library's import action or drop a supported file into the app. ReadAware uses one reader engine for EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, PDF, and supported text and comic formats. A filename extension does not guarantee that an individual file is readable. DRM-protected books are unsupported; ReadAware does not remove DRM or convert your original book into another format. You can also import a whole folder of books at once; each book remembers which folder it came from, so you can ask the Agent to group your shelf by folder.

Your imported books live in the local library. Use search, favorites, and collections to organize them. Opening a book restores its saved reading position.

## Make the reader comfortable

Open the reader's appearance controls for typography, spacing, margins, page colors, and layout. Reflowable books support scrolling and paginated layouts. PDF and comic pages have their own fixed-layout controls; font settings cannot re-typeset text embedded in a page image. Zoom those pages by pinching, or with `Cmd =` and `Cmd −` on macOS (`Ctrl` elsewhere); `Cmd 0` returns to the fit, and the appearance controls choose whether the fit is the page's width or the whole page. In single- and two-page layouts, `Cmd L` or the lock beside the zoom percentage locks a zoomed view, so page turns keep showing the same part of each page. Each book remembers its zoom and your place on the page on this device.

Font choices made for all books are remembered by the current book's language, so switching between languages does not require choosing a font again. A book-specific appearance override still takes priority. The font menu can also import your own TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2, or TTC files; imported fonts sync across your devices. Page turning can use tap zones and, on Android, the volume keys — enable them in Settings → Reading → Page Turning.

Use the table of contents, book search, and navigation history to move around. Exact source locations and extracted text search serve different purposes: a search preview may need a further source lookup before navigation.

## Annotate and ask

Select a passage to highlight it, add a note, or use an available reading action such as explanation, lookup, or translation. AI actions use the model configuration and privacy settings you choose. Notes and highlights remain useful without AI.

Each book has a persistent conversation. Open the chat panel to ask about your reading. The global Context page supports separate conversations across your library. Long-term memory is shared across conversations; creating another thread does not create a separate memory store.

ReadAware assembles relevant reading context, notes, and memories for each turn. Its memory features include reading goals, profile information, book summaries, and entity relationships. Generated content can be incomplete or wrong: review it and use the available correction and forgetting controls.

For fiction, plot summaries and narrative context follow your reading progress to help avoid spoilers. History and biography can use broader context about real events. You can review or correct a book's classification when this distinction is wrong.

If a model request fails, use the retry action to continue the failed step. Tool activity is grouped in the conversation and can be expanded to inspect what the assistant did.

## Connect a model

Open Settings → AI, choose a provider or compatible endpoint, enter your API key, and select models. The smart model handles more demanding chat and synthesis; the fast model handles lighter work. Provider model catalogs and connection tests help you check the setup.

AI requires a working provider connection. BYOK uses your chosen provider and may incur that provider's charges. An available ReadAware AI subscription is another option; see [plans](/pricing). Neither is required for ordinary local reading and annotations.

Review the reading-context and automatic-memory settings before enabling automatic work. Relevant book excerpts and other selected context can leave the device for inference, even though the library and memory are stored locally. See the [privacy policy](/privacy).

## Search the web and view images

In Settings → AI → Web search, enable search, choose TinyFish, Exa, Tavily, SerpAPI, or Brave, and enter that provider's API key. This key is separate from your model key. Run the connection test after changing the provider or credentials.

Search and page reading stay with the selected provider and key. Providers differ: SerpAPI offers search without page reading, and Brave page reading requires access to its LLM Context API. ReadAware does not silently switch to another provider when a capability is unavailable.

The assistant can use web sources and supported image results when they help answer your question. Image previews link back to their sources; support for sending image content to the model depends on the selected model. Search queries, requested URLs, and image requests can leave your device. Review the [privacy policy](/privacy) before enabling these features.

## Connect another assistant

Settings → AI → Local API lets another assistant query your reading data while ReadAware is running. It is off by default. Enable it, use **Copy installation prompt** to install the [ReadAware skill](https://github.com/ahpxex/read-aware/blob/main/skills/readaware/SKILL.md) in your assistant, then use **Copy connection** to supply the local address and access token separately.

The API provides read-only access to library metadata, the table of contents, book text, search, annotations, reading records, and scoped memory. It does not expose settings, model keys, raw files, or write operations. A connected assistant can request unread text, so tell it the reading boundary you want it to respect.

The assistant must be able to make requests on the same computer. A cloud service's own localhost does not reach your desktop, and ordinary browser pages cannot call this API. Keep the connection token private. Reset it to revoke old connections, or turn the API off to stop access. Any data an external assistant sends onward is governed by that assistant's configuration and provider.

## Listen and extend

Read-aloud depends on the reader mode, readable text, and an available voice provider. System voices and voice plugins have different network and configuration needs; scanned pages without usable text are not guaranteed to work.

In Settings → Plugins, enable the tools you want and inspect their permissions. Plugins can add reading actions, commands, themes, content sources, and assistant tools. Availability depends on the package and the contracts supported by your app. Plugins installed from the marketplace update themselves; an update that asks for more permissions waits for your approval there. [Learn how plugins work](/docs/plugins).

The command palette opens with `Cmd K` on macOS or `Ctrl K` elsewhere; shortcuts can be changed in Settings.

## Sync and backup

These solve different problems:

- **Sync** carries encrypted events and files between devices. Configure relay sync in Settings → Data & Sync, or configure a transport such as WebDAV in its plugin settings. Keep the encryption passphrase safe. Sync does not guarantee that every device-local setting, private plugin file, or transient task travels.
- **Backup** creates an encrypted archive for recovery. Since version 0.6.5 ReadAware offers only the full archive; the legacy library-only format has been retired, and older library-only files can no longer be restored. Full restore reviews the archive, asks for its passphrase and choices, and merges supported data through the host's recovery flow.

Relay sync runs automatically while connected. Plugin transports such as WebDAV use **Sync now** in the plugin's settings; they do not run on the relay's automatic schedule. Check the corresponding settings page for connection errors or sign-in requests.

You can keep reading offline. When devices reconnect, the shared progress for a book keeps the furthest recorded position, even if a more recent update from another device is behind it. For example, reaching page 300 offline is not replaced by another device's later record at page 200. ReadAware compares positions within the book, since visible page numbers can vary with layout. Reading time is accumulated separately. This rule does not reset shared progress when you go back to reread earlier pages.

Check the options present in your installed version. A backup's contents, successful save, and ability to restore are separate things; keep a known-good copy before a migration or downgrade.

## Find your data and diagnose problems

The local data directory, sync status, backup actions, and diagnostics are available through Settings. A failed read should show a retryable error when appropriate; a failed save is not a successful change. If reporting a problem, include the app version, operating system, steps to reproduce, and a reviewed diagnostics export.

[Download and install](/docs/install) · [Plugin system](/docs/plugins) · [Privacy](/privacy)

pluginsOverview.metaDescription: Understand ReadAware plugin domains, contributions, services, object grants, host-rendered UI, and the current development contract.
pluginsOverview.body:
# Plugin system

ReadAware plugins compose capabilities the desktop host exposes. They can work with books, reading state, annotations, conversations, and memory; add actions and providers; and use bounded host services.

This reference follows the development source. Match capability requirements to your installed app before building or publishing.

## Choose a capability family

| Family | Use it for | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Domains** | ReadAware-owned data and behavior | Library, reading, annotations, conversations, settings, memory |
| **Contributions** | New actions, choices, or provider implementations | Commands, context actions, voices, content sources, assistant tools, themes |
| **Services** | Host operations and plugin-private facilities | Resources, network, inference, storage, schedules, jobs, transactions |
| **Schemas** | Data the host renders or interprets | Views, settings forms, themes |

Use the [Capabilities Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) to search actual methods, understand boundaries, and start a manifest. The API reference explains [how the families compose](/docs/plugins/api).

## Start from the reader's task

- **Find and navigate:** use Library source search and range reads, then Reading navigation with the current session guard.
- **Collect and review notes:** query or observe Annotations; conditional mutations preserve newer edits.
- **Work with reading memory:** use Memory queries and authorized commands for memories, classification, profiles, entities, graphs, and context bundles.
- **Assist a conversation:** read authorized transcripts and summaries, propose a turn for host approval, or register an assistant tool.
- **Automate a workflow:** combine schedules, scoped change cursors, supported durable jobs, and local transactions.
- **Bring in outside content:** use origin-scoped network access, content providers, and sealed resources instead of filesystem or browser escape hatches.

## Permissions, versions, and object grants

These are separate checks:

1. `requires` declares compatible capability versions.
2. `permissions`, `settingsAccess`, and `networkAccess` declare authority.
3. The user's book grant limits the actor to all books, the current book, or a specified book.
4. Lifecycle and current runtime conditions determine whether a particular operation is available now.

A permission-free service can still require another domain grant for a specific method. A successful availability query is a hint, not permission to bypass the execution check.

## Host-rendered interfaces

Plugins return structured views and callbacks. ReadAware owns rendering, focus, navigation, loading and error states, themes, and cleanup. Views can include lists, forms, detail layouts, and bounded blocks, with live updates through the public view contract.

Plugins do not mount React, arbitrary HTML, CSS, iframes, or a DOM. Use a supported contribution point for new UI behavior.

## Isolation and lifecycle

Each plugin runs in a module Worker. It receives no direct Tauri, SQLite, filesystem, process, or DOM access. Network and storage use the host-mediated context.

Activation stages registrations and permits supported reads; business writes and external side effects begin from active handlers. A private-data migration runs with storage-only authority. Failed activation or migration is rolled back before a candidate replaces the current runtime.

Marketplace plugins update automatically when a new release asks for no authority beyond what the user approved — permissions, settings access and network origins; anything more waits for consent. Plugins installed from a folder or zip are never replaced by a marketplace listing.

Installation is still a software trust decision. Review the package source, requested authority, network destinations, and data handling.

## Learn from first-party plugins

The source tree contains working examples such as Jumper, Dictionary, and Sentence Reader, alongside bundled plugins. Source examples are not a promise that every package ships in every release.

[Build a plugin](/docs/plugins/develop) · [API reference](/docs/plugins/api) · [Publishing](/docs/plugins/publishing)

pluginsDevelop.metaDescription: Build a small ReadAware command, declare compatible capabilities and permissions, then test the package in the desktop app.
pluginsDevelop.body:
# Build a plugin

Begin with one useful action. Keep compatibility, authority, and runtime behavior visible as you add capabilities.

## Get the template and types

The [public plugin repository](https://github.com/ahpxex/readaware-plugins) contains the template, the contract, the registry, and its checks. Its `types/plugin-api.d.ts` and `types/host-capabilities.json` are generated from the latest ReadAware release named in their headers: the first is the complete contract, imported as `@readaware/plugin-api`; the second lists each capability's version and the permissions that unlock it. Choose `requires` ranges from it. This site documents the development contract, which can be ahead of that release; the [Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) shows each capability's version in the latest release.

Use Bun, at the version in `.bun-version`. Run `bun install`, copy `template/` to `plugins/<your-plugin-id>/`, and keep the directory name equal to the manifest ID.

## Build with a coding agent

Give the agent a checkout of the plugin repository and point it to [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ahpxex/readaware-plugins/blob/main/AGENTS.md). That single file covers the workflow, manifest rules, the sandbox, testing, a verified worked example, and the checks CI runs. The validator applies the app's install checks against the latest release, so an agent can confirm compatibility without the app.

## A minimal command

This example registers a command during activation and performs its UI effect only when the user runs it.

```json
{
  "id": "hello-reader",
  "name": "Hello Reader",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "main": "main.js",
  "requires": {
    "contributions": { "commands": "^1.1.0" },
    "services": { "ui": "^1.17.0" }
  }
}
```

```typescript
export default {
  activate(ctx) {
    ctx.contributions.commands.register({
      id: "hello",
      title: "Say hello",
      run: () => ctx.services.ui.showToast("Hello, reader!"),
    });
  },
};
```

Compile the entry module to a self-contained `main.js`. The manifest above requires the versions in the latest release; use older ranges only after checking and testing those contracts.

## Commands and shortcuts

Commands appear in the command palette and in Settings → Shortcuts, where users can bind or rebind any of them. A command may suggest a binding with `defaultShortcut`, a chord such as `{ "key": "s", "mod": true, "shift": true }`; `mod` is ⌘ on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Avoid the built-in chords listed under `builtInShortcuts` in `types/host-capabilities.json`: when two shortcuts share a chord, pressing it runs neither until the user rebinds one. Shortcuts do not fire while the user is typing.

## Add the smallest useful authority

Use the [Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) to find a method and copy its starting manifest fragment. A fragment declares a capability; complete the grants needed by the particular operation.

- Reading library data requires `library:read`; changing it requires `library:write`.
- Settings use exact `settingsAccess` paths and operations.
- Arbitrary HTTP needs `service:network` plus allowed `networkAccess.origins`.
- A reader-related method in a permission-free UI service may still need `reading:read` or `reading:write`.
- Book grants are selected through host consent and exposed in `ctx.grants.book`; a manifest cannot give itself access to another book.

Inspect `ctx.capabilities` and handle absent optional namespaces. Keep ReadAware-owned data in its domains; plugin storage is for your own records, settings, and checkpoints.

## Work with observations and cancellation

Release handles when you no longer need them. For supported calls, pass an `AbortSignal` and await the actual outcome. Cancellation does not undo a write or remote side effect that already happened.

An automatic reaction uses `ctx.withEvent(delivery)` for resulting work, including after an `await`. Give causal subscriptions a stable `ruleId` where the contract requires it. User-initiated actions use the original activation context. This lets the host detect loops without conflating independent actions.

## Build and install locally

Run the public plugin repository's checks from its root. `bun run check` is what CI runs: the validator, the typecheck, the tests, and a rebuild that must match each committed `main.js`.

```bash
bun install
bun run build
bun run check
```

Open ReadAware → Settings → Plugins → Install plugin, select the built folder, and review the consent summary. Exercise the feature in the desktop app. Rebuild and reinstall to check an update.

## Version private data

`schemaVersion` is independent of the package version. When the stored KV or document shape changes, supply the supported upgrade and downgrade transitions through `migrate(storageCtx, change)`.

Migration receives storage-only authority. Test a failed transition as well as success: the prior package and committed data must remain usable. Avoid adding an unnecessary schema change for ordinary code updates.

## Test the boundaries your feature uses

Check its actual Worker/Tauri behavior, permission and book-scope refusals, cancellation, disable/re-enable, and failure recovery. For a UI plugin, include keyboard navigation, long text, and narrow windows. For a data-changing plugin, include concurrent edits and restart where persistence matters.

Schedules run while the app is open; durable jobs support only the host's typed plans. Neither is a general background process or arbitrary-code job runner. [The API reference](/docs/plugins/api) describes these limits.

## Publish

Once the built package works with its declared minimum contracts, follow [Publishing](/docs/plugins/publishing).

pluginsCapabilities.metaDescription: Search the current ReadAware plugin catalog and API methods, filter by task or authority, and inspect manifest requirements.
pluginsCapabilities.body:
# Capabilities Explorer

Find the contracts for what you want to build. Search a task, capability, permission, or exact API method; narrow by topic, family, or authority. Open an entry for its methods, boundaries, and a copyable manifest fragment.

The catalog follows the **development source**, which may be newer than the latest download. Versions come from the host catalog and methods from the public TypeScript contract. Your installed app's `ctx.capabilities`, book grant, and runtime checks determine what you can actually call.

READAWARE_CAPABILITY_BROWSER_SLOT

## Read authority correctly

A capability version is a compatibility requirement. A permission authorizes access. Book grants, exact Settings paths, network origins, lifecycle, and method-specific checks further narrow that access.

**No extra permission** describes the capability's base grant. It does not remove another domain's permissions from a method or bypass host confirmation. `readerModes` remains bundled-only. Declarative themes and fonts are supplied through the manifest.

## Manifest preview

Paste your manifest to inspect permissions, Settings grants, network origins, and version requirements together. This check runs locally against the catalog shown above. It cannot prove installation, runtime availability, or compatibility with an older app.

READAWARE_PERMISSION_PREVIEW_SLOT

## Continue building

Use [Build a plugin](/docs/plugins/develop) for a working starting point and the [API reference](/docs/plugins/api) for scope, lifecycle, observations, jobs, and transaction semantics. Check a matching app build before [publishing](/docs/plugins/publishing).

pluginsApi.metaDescription: The current ReadAware development API: six domains, contributions, host services, permissions, book scopes, observations, jobs, and transactions.
pluginsApi.body:
# Plugin API reference

This page explains the development contract, which can be ahead of the latest release. The complete reference at the end lists every capability with its development version and its version in the latest release, the permission it needs, and each method's resolved signature and documentation. The [Capabilities Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) offers the same catalog interactively. The public plugin repository's types match the latest release.

## Package and manifest

A plugin contains `manifest.json` and a self-contained ES module, normally `main.js`. Keep source and required assets with the package for review.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `name`, `version` | Stable namespace, display name, and package version. The ID matches the folder name. |
| `schemaVersion` | Positive integer for the plugin's private data schema; independent of package version. |
| `requires` | Capability IDs and semver ranges, grouped into `domains`, `contributions`, `services`, and `schemas`. |
| `permissions` | Semantic authority, such as `library:read` or `service:llm`. |
| `settingsAccess` | Separate `discover`, `read`, and `write` grants for exact paths or explicit section groups. |
| `networkAccess` | Allowed HTTP(S) origins for Network 2.x; required alongside `service:network`. |
| `minAppVersion` | Optional app-version floor, in addition to capability requirements. |
| `main` | Relative entry module; defaults to `main.js`. |
| `settings`, `schedules`, `themes`, `fonts` | Host-interpreted declarations. |
| `services` | Versioned, typed module service exports for cross-plugin calls. |

There is no manifest field that grants arbitrary filesystem, SQL, DOM, or native IPC access.

## Context and object scope

The host calls `activate(ctx)` with `ctx.domains`, `ctx.contributions`, and `ctx.services`, plus the manifest, locale, app version, lifecycle phase, capability versions, and immutable book grant.

`ctx.grants.book` is `all`, `current`, or a specified `book`. The host selects it through consent. Reading, memory, conversations, commands, and resources preserve that scope across calls and callbacks. A current-book change can invalidate outstanding reads, handles, proposals, and observations.

Domain write permission includes read. Settings grants remain separate by operation. Permission-gated namespaces or methods can be absent; host-side checks still run on every call. Use `ctx.services.session.operationAvailability(...)` for supported preflight queries, and handle execution failure even after a positive result.

## Domains

| Domain | Available work | Boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `library` | Books and collections, TOCs, exact location search, ranges, references and images, imports, text tasks, metadata, duplicate merges, and removal. | Source versions, book scope, bounded reads, actor-owned tasks, and separate file-cleanup receipts. |
| `reading` | Session snapshots, navigation, selection, playback and mode controls, progress, reading time and insights. | Current session guards, settled versus pending state, provider availability, and cancellation. |
| `annotations` | Pages, inspection and observations; create highlights or notes; conditional edit/delete batches. | Use the revision observed before the user's decision. Captured ranges also require Library access. |
| `conversations` | Authorized transcripts, stored summaries, runtime and turn-request state; thread controls and proposed turns. | Host approval starts a proposed turn. Global-thread operations require all-books access. Plugins do not replace the chat runtime. |
| `settings` | Catalog discovery, resolved snapshots, options, model metadata, observation, updates and reading resets. | Exact paths, target policy, and additional authority for external provider work. |
| `memory` | Search and pages, inspection, correction/forgetting, profiles, entities, classification, graphs and tasks, context archives. | Book grants and conditional revisions. Global identity/profile operations require all-books access; generation also needs model authority. |

### Source text and navigation

Use `library.queries.books.searchLocations` for navigable source matches and `readRange` for bounded source text. Preserve the returned source version and location. Derived `searchText` hits are previews, not interchangeable navigation anchors. Explicit text preparation returns a task whose progress and outcome must be observed.

### Conditional writes

Inspect the current object and retain its revision before showing an edit. Submit the conditional mutation against that revision. On conflict, reread and let the user decide; silently replacing the expected revision would overwrite another change.

`annotations.commands.applyChanges`, memory mutations, private document commits, and transaction previews each have their own typed contract. Ordinary commands are not automatically undoable or distributed transactions.

### Observations and reactions

Use authorized observations for current state and committed subscriptions for events. A sequence number can order deliveries without being a database cursor or a conditional-write revision. Failed observations must remain distinguishable from empty results.

Use `ctx.withEvent(delivery)` for automatic follow-up work and stable rule IDs on causal subscriptions where required. Preserve the bound context through asynchronous calls. The host rejects causal cycles and expired deliveries; independent user actions use the original context.

## Contributions

| Contribution | What the plugin supplies |
| --- | --- |
| `selectionActions`, `headerActions`, `contextActions`, `commands`, `uriHandlers` | Actions at typed host surfaces, palette commands, and namespaced URI handling. |
| `settingsOptions` | Dynamic options for a declared plugin setting. |
| `voiceProviders`, `contentProviders`, `readerModes` | Audio synthesis, virtual-book content, and bundled reader segmentation modes. |
| `agentTools`, `agentContextProviders`, `agentRetrievalProviders` | Tools, bounded per-turn context, and searchable plugin-owned sources. |
| `memoryCandidateProviders` | Candidate memories for host validation and acceptance. |
| `themes`, `fonts` | Manifest-declared appearance choices. |
| `syncTransports` | Storage of opaque encrypted sync envelopes and meta objects. |

Actions can update their owned visible/enabled/checked state where supported. Registrations and disposables belong to one activation. Returning a view does not grant the callback extra domain authority.

Memory candidates and direct Memory commands are distinct paths: candidates go through host acceptance, while direct commands require the appropriate Memory grant and revision. Neither permits injecting system rules or replacing the core agent.

## Host services

| Service | Use it for | Key limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storage` | Private KV, document collections, conditional commits, pages, observations and usage policies. | Plugin namespace and quotas; stale cursors require a fresh baseline. |
| `resources` | User-picked files/directories, sealed byte handles, exports, images and private binary assets. | No ambient paths. Handles have owners, limits and lifetimes. |
| `secrets` | Plugin-private encrypted credential slots. | No access to another plugin's secrets. |
| `network` | Origin-scoped HTTP, bounded buffered requests and streaming. | Every redirect is checked; no automatic replay of arbitrary writes. |
| `llm` | Text or structured inference, streaming, image resources, request receipts and budgets. | User configuration, privacy rules, cancellation, and host/provider limits. |
| `clipboard` | Write text or a sealed image. | Explicit permission and supported resource type. |
| `ui` | Views, toast, native save/open flows, workspace and command navigation, reader panels and windows. | Method-specific domain grants and host-owned presentation. |
| `session` | Non-sensitive environment metadata and operation availability. | No old reading-session subscription; use the Reading domain. |
| `schedules` | Declared recurring handlers and owned deferred requests. | Work runs while the app is open; timing is not exact. |
| `jobs` | Supported durable plans, checkpoints, observation and control. | Typed host operations, not arbitrary JavaScript execution. |
| `changes` | Scoped persistent change cursors. | Reload hints, not a raw event log or historical values. |
| `transactions` | Preview, commit, receipt lookup and conditional undo preview. | Supported local operations and original grants; unknown outcomes require receipt lookup. |
| `plugins` | Inspect registrations, observe changes, discover and invoke typed plugin services. | Caller/callee authority intersection, scope, versions, and isolated service execution. |
| `maintenance` | Status and host-owned backup, connection-test and update flows. | The host keeps credentials, file dialogs and consequential confirmation. |
| `sync` | Authorized sync status, backlog and host-managed account or sync flows. | No encryption keys or raw account credentials. |
| `diagnostics`, `logging` | Reviewed diagnostic exports and bounded structured developer events. | No arbitrary content, secrets or automatic reporting through the log API. |

### Network and inference

Network 2.x needs both a semantic permission and explicit origins:

```json
{
  "requires": { "services": { "network": "^2.2.0" } },
  "permissions": ["service:network"],
  "networkAccess": { "origins": ["https://api.example.com"] }
}
```

Replace the example origin with the endpoint you actually use. Origins include scheme, host and port; they are not URL paths or subdomain globs. Redirects must remain authorized. Streaming callers close owned streams when done. Optional safe retry is limited to supported read requests before a response is delivered; cancellation does not roll back a remote side effect.

For inference, use `readingContext` for book context so the host can apply privacy and scope rules. Use sealed resource IDs for supported images. Request metadata and output budgets help control work; they are not a billing statement or a guarantee of provider compliance.

### Background work and transactions

Use a schedule to arrange a handler invocation, an owned deferred request for later work while the app runs, and a durable job only when its typed plan supports the operation. Restart recovery can require attention rather than blindly repeating an uncertain external result.

Transactions combine supported settings, private-document and domain operations under the original grants. Preview freezes the proposed work; commit consumes that preview. After an unknown response, query the receipt before retrying. Undo is conditional on the state still matching the prior result.

### Cross-plugin services

Declare service ID, version, scope, required permissions, and input/output schemas in the provider manifest, and export its handler in the module's `services` object. Discover and call it through the Plugins service. The host runs a fresh isolated service realm with intersected authority; it does not activate the provider's ordinary UI runtime for the call. Agent-originated calls retain their approval requirement.

## Views, settings, themes and fonts

Plugins return declarative view data. The host renders lists, forms, markdown, details and supported block layouts. Use typed view results and live view updates; keep loading, conflict, empty and error states distinct. No React, DOM, iframe or arbitrary CSS is available to plugin code.

Settings fields are rendered by the host. Secret fields write into encrypted secret slots and do not become ordinary form values or model-visible settings. Supplying a theme or font needs `ui:themes`; selecting one uses the corresponding Settings write grant.

## Lifecycle and compatibility

1. **Activating:** supported reads and registrations; staged contributions are not yet visible.
2. **Migrating:** private storage only, before committing a changed schema.
3. **Active:** promoted handlers may use granted capabilities.

The host health-checks and promotes a candidate after activation and any migration succeed. Failure restores the previous package and data. Unload releases registrations, callbacks and owned resources; durable data follows its separate retention contract. In current development, uninstall removes private document collections and binary assets while retaining the defined KV/secret/schema state for reinstall.

Declare each used capability and schema independently. A version number proves contract compatibility, not that every operating system, provider or failure case has passed end-to-end acceptance. Verify the actual desktop workflow you ship.

[Build a plugin](/docs/plugins/develop) · [Capabilities Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) · [Publishing](/docs/plugins/publishing)

## Complete reference

Every capability of the development contract, grouped by family. A plugin meant for the app people use today should require the version listed for the latest release.

pluginsPublishing.body:
# Publishing a plugin

The [public plugin repository](https://github.com/ahpxex/readaware-plugins) hosts marketplace packages and accepts changes through pull requests. Use its current contribution instructions and validator when preparing a submission.

## Match the app you support

The development catalog can be ahead of the latest released app. The repository's `types/host-capabilities.json` describes that release, and its validator rejects `requires` ranges the release cannot satisfy. A package that needs a new capability must wait for a compatible host release; changing only `minAppVersion` does not create the missing API.

Use the [Capabilities Explorer](/docs/plugins/capabilities) to inspect methods and versions, then declare the smallest compatible set you have actually tested.

## Make the package reviewable

Commit `manifest.json`, readable source, the built self-contained `main.js`, and required runtime assets. Keep the folder name equal to the manifest ID. Do not load remote executable code or depend on files outside the package.

```tree
plugins/my-plugin/
  manifest.json
  main.js
  package.json
  src/main.ts
  src/main.test.ts
  assets/
```

## Check behavior and authority

- Explain the feature, its entry points, and why each permission is needed.
- Declare exact Settings grants and required network origins. Explain which data goes to external services.
- Test book scope, absent permissions, cancellation, disable/re-enable, and the actual desktop UI.
- Keep activation declarative and migrations storage-only.
- Check private data retention, quotas, and cleanup of active resources.
- For updates, exercise an existing installation with realistic data, including a failed migration and recovery.

The local manifest preview helps identify compatibility and authority mistakes. It does not replace the repository validator, desktop testing, or review.

## Build and submit

Run the public repository's checks from its root; `bun run check` is what CI runs on your pull request:

```bash
bun install
bun run build
bun run check
```

Add the matching registry entry according to the repository's current schema and ordering. Open a pull request describing the final behavior, tested app and capability versions, private data, external services, and permission changes. Include reproducible verification steps.

## Updates

Bump the package version in the manifest and registry. Change `schemaVersion` only for a private-data schema change, with its migration in the same package. A request for more authority needs a clear explanation and a usable refusal path.

Signing, publisher identity, package integrity, review provenance and revocation are separate distribution concerns. State the controls that actually apply to the package; Worker isolation alone is not a guarantee about arbitrary code.

domains__library.purpose: Inspect books, source text, TOCs, exact locations, ranges, images and collections; import, organize and manage text tasks.
domains__library.hostOwns: Source versions, book scope, file ownership, event-sourced writes and task receipts.

domains__reading.purpose: Observe reading sessions, navigate and select text, control playback and modes, and query progress, time and insights.
domains__reading.hostOwns: Current-session guards, reader lifecycle, settled state, providers and completion semantics.

domains__annotations.purpose: Page, inspect and observe highlights and notes; create them or apply revision-checked edits and deletes.
domains__annotations.hostOwns: Captured source validation, conditional revisions, attribution and atomic persistence.

domains__conversations.purpose: Read authorized transcripts, summaries and runtime state; propose turns, manage threads and use approved stop or clear controls.
domains__conversations.hostOwns: Host approval and generation, book grants, global-thread boundaries and actor-owned requests.

domains__settings.purpose: Discover exact setting paths and options, read settled snapshots, observe changes and update supported targets.
domains__settings.hostOwns: Path grants, secret exclusion, target validation, persistence and effects; provider work may need network authority.

domains__memory.purpose: Search, page, inspect and correct memories; work with profiles, entities, classification, graphs and versioned context bundles.
domains__memory.hostOwns: Book and global scope, conditional writes, spoiler boundaries, generation authority and immutable context versions.

contributions__uriHandlers.purpose: Handle namespaced ReadAware URI invocations through a registered action.
contributions__uriHandlers.hostOwns: URI routing, validation, consent and handler lifecycle; no arbitrary scheme takeover.

contributions__selectionActions.purpose: Add actions for captured selection, annotation or navigator input.
contributions__selectionActions.hostOwns: Menu placement, captured context, invocation state and existing domain grants.

contributions__headerActions.purpose: Add reader, library or agent header actions with host-rendered views.
contributions__headerActions.hostOwns: Placement, focus, view navigation, loading and cleanup.

contributions__contextActions.purpose: Add typed actions for supported book or collection context surfaces.
contributions__contextActions.hostOwns: Target identity, supported surfaces, invocation and current authority.

contributions__commands.purpose: Add namespaced command-palette actions and update their owned state.
contributions__commands.hostOwns: Registry ownership, shortcuts, availability and result presentation.

contributions__settingsOptions.purpose: Resolve dynamic choices for a declared plugin setting.
contributions__settingsOptions.hostOwns: Form rendering, saved non-secret values, bounded results and validation.

contributions__settingsPage.purpose: Register one declarative page that replaces the plugin's manifest settings form in its own Settings section.
contributions__settingsPage.hostOwns: The Settings section and navigation, view rendering and validation, and retiring open views on disable.

contributions__voiceProviders.purpose: Provide voice choices and encoded audio for read-aloud.
contributions__voiceProviders.hostOwns: Playback, pacing, prefetch, highlighting and cancellation.

contributions__contentProviders.purpose: Provide sections for virtual books such as saved feeds.
contributions__contentProviders.hostOwns: Library binding, source invalidation, reading state and navigation.

contributions__readerModes.purpose: Supply bounded sentence or paragraph segmentation in bundled plugins.
contributions__readerModes.hostOwns: Reader rendering, lifecycle, navigation and privileged mode admission.

contributions__agentTools.purpose: Register namespaced tools that the reading assistant can discover and call.
contributions__agentTools.hostOwns: Tool visibility, approval, book scope, orchestration and transcript UI.

contributions__agentContextProviders.purpose: Supply bounded per-turn reference blocks and declared reading-intent sources.
contributions__agentContextProviders.hostOwns: Provenance, durable-source rules, clipping, placement and lifetime.

contributions__agentRetrievalProviders.purpose: Expose searchable plugin-owned sources to the assistant.
contributions__agentRetrievalProviders.hostOwns: Query schema, result limits, clipping and namespaced tool discovery.

contributions__memoryCandidateProviders.purpose: Propose facts, preferences, insights or summaries for memory acceptance.
contributions__memoryCandidateProviders.hostOwns: Scope validation, deduplication, acceptance and durable writes.

contributions__themes.purpose: Declare semantic app and reader theme choices in the manifest.
contributions__themes.hostOwns: Token validation, CSS generation and application only after selection.

contributions__fonts.purpose: Declare font metadata and packaged font assets.
contributions__fonts.hostOwns: Asset validation, loading, picker entries and active selection.

contributions__syncTransports.purpose: Store and retrieve opaque encrypted events, blobs and key-material meta objects on an alternative remote.
contributions__syncTransports.hostOwns: Encryption, keys, cursors, merge, scheduling and passphrase flows.

services__storage.purpose: Use private KV and document collections, pages, observations, conditional commits and quota policies.
services__storage.hostOwns: Namespace isolation, revision checks, snapshots and retention rules.

services__secrets.purpose: Read and write credentials in plugin-private encrypted slots.
services__secrets.hostOwns: Encryption and namespace isolation; no other plugin or app credentials.

services__ui.purpose: Publish views, show toast, save or open resources, navigate workspaces and commands, and control supported reader panels and windows.
services__ui.hostOwns: Typed surfaces, per-method domain grants, host confirmation, focus and lifecycle.

services__schedules.purpose: Bind declared recurring handlers, inspect and control schedules, and manage owned deferred requests.
services__schedules.hostOwns: Open-app execution, timing, ownership, coalescing and cancellation semantics.

services__jobs.purpose: Start, inspect and control durable plans built from supported host operations.
services__jobs.hostOwns: Checkpoints, restart recovery, original authority and uncertain-outcome handling; no arbitrary code jobs.

services__changes.purpose: Open and read scoped change cursors that can be persisted across restarts.
services__changes.hostOwns: Grant-filtered reload hints, cursor expiry and restore invalidation; no raw event values.

services__transactions.purpose: Preview and commit supported local changes, inspect receipts and preview conditional undo.
services__transactions.hostOwns: Atomicity, frozen previews, revision checks and the original domain and Settings grants.

services__session.purpose: Read environment metadata and check availability of supported operations.
services__session.hostOwns: No reading-session subscription or private account state; execution always rechecks conditions.

services__plugins.purpose: Inspect installed plugins and registrations, observe changes, and discover or call typed plugin services.
services__plugins.hostOwns: Activation identity, caller/callee authority intersection, book scope and service isolation.

services__maintenance.purpose: Inspect maintenance state and enter host-owned backup, connection-test, update or settings flows.
services__maintenance.hostOwns: Credentials, confirmation, recovery, native dialogs and actual completion receipts.

services__diagnostics.purpose: Request supported diagnostic export or reporting flows.
services__diagnostics.hostOwns: Permission, user review, redaction and native delivery; no silent arbitrary uploads.

services__logging.purpose: Write bounded structured developer events and inspect logging policy.
services__logging.hostOwns: Rate limits and field vocabulary; no arbitrary user text, secrets, paths or stack traces.

services__resources.purpose: Pick files and directories, read or create sealed resources, export data, and store private binary assets.
services__resources.hostOwns: Opaque ownership, size and lifetime limits, book grants, native confirmation and cleanup.

services__sync.purpose: Observe sync status and backlog, request sync, and enter host-managed account or connection flows.
services__sync.hostOwns: Encryption keys, credentials, sensitive UI and transport lifecycle.

services__network.purpose: Make origin-scoped HTTP requests or read bounded streams, with opt-in safe retries.
services__network.hostOwns: Origin and redirect checks, quotas, deadlines, cancellation and no implicit replay of writes.

services__llm.purpose: Request text, structured or streaming inference, use sealed image resources, and track request metadata and budgets.
services__llm.hostOwns: User model configuration, privacy filtering, scope, cancellation and provider limits.

services__clipboard.purpose: Write text or a supported sealed image to the system clipboard.
services__clipboard.hostOwns: Permission, resource ownership, host image decoding and OS delivery.

schemas__views.purpose: Describe host-rendered lists, forms, details, markdown and supported block layouts.
schemas__views.hostOwns: Schema validation, rendering, focus, loading states and callbacks.

schemas__settings.purpose: Declare typed plugin settings, conditional fields and dynamic option references.
schemas__settings.hostOwns: Control rendering, value validation and secret separation.

schemas__themes.purpose: Describe semantic application and reader palettes.
schemas__themes.hostOwns: The host token vocabulary, safe values and selection; theme authority still requires ui:themes.
